description: The third arm of the read ladder in 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT :345-369, and the folder's closing width and FILLER audit. THE LADDER, ARM BY ARM. :346 READ DALYTRAN-FILE INTO DALYTRAN-RECORD is followed by a three-way test on DALYTRAN-STATUS: :347 '00' takes :348 MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT, :351 '10' takes :352 MOVE 16, and anything else takes :354 MOVE 12. The second guard then reads APPL-RESULT through the program's only two 88-levels, APPL-AOK VALUE 0 and APPL-EOF VALUE 16 at :143-144: :357 IF APPL-AOK is false at 12, :360 IF APPL-EOF is false at 12, so the ELSE at :362 runs its four statements in order - :363 DISPLAY 'ERROR READING DALYTRAN FILE', :364 MOVE DALYTRAN-STATUS TO IO-STATUS, :365 PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, :366 PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. All three arms of this one paragraph are now driven: case01 takes '00' on the same seed, case13 takes '10' on an empty dataset, and this case takes the third, which completes gate G47 for this call site. Note that the arms are an ordered nested-IF ladder and not an EVALUATE - CBTRN02C contains zero EVALUATE statements and zero GO TOs - so gate G30's ordering requirement applies to the IF chain, and the third arm is reachable only because the first two are tested for equality against specific literals rather than for a range. THE STATUS LINE, CHARACTER BY CHARACTER. The injected status is '30', the permanent-error file status. IO-STATUS is a group of two PIC X items, IO-STAT1 and IO-STAT2 at :132-133, and IO-STATUS-04 at :138-140 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999, so the rendered image is exactly FOUR characters wide and can never be more. 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS :714-727 tests IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9' at :715-716. '30' is two digits, so the COBOL class condition holds and IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC is FALSE; IO-STAT1 is '3' and not '9'; both halves of the condition are false, so the first arm is skipped and the ELSE at :722-725 runs. :723 MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 fills all four characters, :724 MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2) overlays the two status characters at one-based positions three and four, giving 0030, and :725 DISPLAY 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' IO-STATUS-04 concatenates the twenty-character literal with the four-character field and NOTHING BETWEEN THEM, so the line is FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0030 - positions 1-20 the literal, 21-24 the image, no space at the join. The trailing NNNN belongs to the COBOL literal and is not a placeholder awaiting substitution. This is the same arm case18 reaches with '22' rendering NNNN0022; case14 and case17 reach the other arm, where a '9' first character renders NNNN9000. THE ABEND. 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM :707-711 displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :708, moves 0 to TIMING at :709 and 999 to ABCODE at :710 - both PIC S9(9) BINARY at :147-148 - and calls CEE3ABD at :711, which does not return. APPL-RESULT is 12 at that moment. THE RETURN CODE AND WHERE 12 COMES FROM. CBTRN02C executes no MOVE ... TO RETURN-CODE on any abend path; its single such statement is the literal 4 at :230, which sits downstream of END-PERFORM and is unreachable here. The value asserted is the one the abend itself carries: the translation raises common.AbendException through the job's shared failure tail, which passes the current APPL-RESULT as the RETURN-CODE - 12, AbendException.RETURN_CODE_IO_ERROR, the value :354 moved - alongside ABCODE 999 and TIMING 0 from :710 and :709. Twelve sits inside the domain the model permits, 0, 3, 4, 8, 12 and 16, and satisfies gate G35. Note what it displaces: this seed rejects nothing, so a completed run would have ended at 0. WHAT THE ABEND PREVENTS, EXHAUSTIVELY. The abend fires INSIDE 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT, which the mainline performs at :204, so control never returns to the loop body and never leaves the loop. None of the following runs: the :205 IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' guard and everything inside it for record 2 - ADD 1 TO WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT at :206, MOVE 0 TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON at :208, MOVE SPACES at :209, PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN at :210, and neither PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION at :212 nor ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT at :214 with PERFORM 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC at :215; the END-PERFORM at :219; the six closes 9000-DALYTRAN-CLOSE :221, 9100-TRANFILE-CLOSE :222, 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE :223, 9300-DALYREJS-CLOSE :224, 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE :225 and 9500-TCATBALF-CLOSE :226; both count lines, DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT at :227 and DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :' WS-REJECT-COUNT at :228; the IF WS-REJECT-COUNT > 0 / MOVE 4 TO RETURN-CODE / END-IF at :229-231; DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN02C' at :232; and GOBACK at :234. So WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT IS NOT INCREMENTED FOR RECORD 2: the ADD at :206 sits after the PERFORM at :204 and inside the :205 guard, and the abend happens before either is reached. It stands at 1 when the program dies, and neither count line is ever displayed, so the four-entry message list is the whole assertion rather than an abbreviation of a longer one. WHAT RECORD 1 COMMITTED, AND WHY IT STAYS COMMITTED. Record 1 is exactly case01's transaction and every derived value here agrees with it. Its read reported '00', :206 counted it, and 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN passed all three checks: 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF :380 read card 4859452612877065 and found XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000007; 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT :393 read that account; COMPUTE WS-TEMP-BAL = ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT - ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT + DALYTRAN-AMT at :403-405 is 0.00 - 0.00 + 504.77 = 504.77; IF ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT >= WS-TEMP-BAL at :407 is 2065.00 >= 504.77, true; and IF ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE >= DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS (1:10) at :414 is '2024-12-13' >= '2022-06-10', true. Reason 0, so :212 performed 2000-POST-TRANSACTION :424, which moves twelve fields at :425-436, composes TRAN-PROC-TS at :437-438, and then performs its three updates in exactly this order: 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL at :440, 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC at :441, 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE at :442. The category-balance key 00000000007010001 was present, so :474's keyed read reported '00', WS-CREATE-TRANCAT-REC stayed 'N', the fork at :495 took :498 rather than :496, NO 'Creating.' line was displayed, and 2700-B-UPDATE-TCATBAL-REC :526 added 504.77 to 0.00 at :527 and rewrote at :528. 2800 added 504.77 to ACCT-CURR-BAL at :547 giving 697.77, took the DALYTRAN-AMT >= 0 arm at :548 so ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT became 504.77 while ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT stayed 0.00, and rewrote at :554. 2900 wrote the 350-byte TRAN-RECORD at :564, which is TRANFILE row 0. NOTHING IS ROLLED BACK. All three of those writes are asserted here in their committed form - TRAN-CAT-BAL 504.77, ACCT-CURR-BAL 697.77, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT 504.77 and one TRANFILE row - because the COBOL has no unit of recovery around a record: app/jcl/POSTTRAN.jcl declares the VSAM datasets DISP=SHR with no RECOVERY, each REWRITE and WRITE takes effect as it is issued, and a later abend does not undo an earlier one. This is the sharpest assertion in the case and it is a negative one: if a chunk rollback were ever introduced these three would read 0.00, 193.00 and no row at all, and the case would fail on the values rather than on the messages (practice B5). THE WIDTH AND FILLER AUDIT. Every width below is summed from its copybook, field by field, and the bolded span in each is the trailing FILLER; omit any one of them and the total is short and every subsequent offset is wrong, which is precisely what gate G21 exists to catch and what FieldDiffer's width-mismatch diff kind reports. DalyTranRecord, CVTRA06Y: 16 + 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 16 + 26 + 26 + FILLER 20 = 350. TranRecord, CVTRA05Y: the identical shape under the TRAN- prefix, 14 items and not 15 - the twelve fields :425-436 copies, TRAN-PROC-TS, and FILLER - = 350. TranCatBalRecord, CVTRA01Y: the 17-byte TRAN-CAT-KEY as 11 + 2 + 4, then 11, then FILLER 22 = 50. AccountRecord, CVACT01Y: 11 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + FILLER 178 = 300. CardXrefRecord, CVACT03Y: 16 + 9 + 11 = 36 on disk, against a declared 50 that ends in FILLER X(14). The DALYREJS image, from REJECT-RECORD at :176-178 and WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER at :180-182: 350 + (4 + 76) = 430, which is the LRECL app/jcl/POSTTRAN.jcl:36 declares, and it is asserted at zero rows on the WRITES channel because nothing was rejected and because DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) names DELETE as the abnormal disposition, so a step that abends leaves no generation behind. These sums are literal byte counts with no nibble packing, because not one of the 28 copybooks in this repository declares COMP-3 or PACKED-DECIMAL - every persisted numeric field is zoned DISPLAY, which is what makes a mechanical audit possible at all. WHAT EACH FILLER HOLDS, AND WHY IT IS NOT ALWAYS SPACES. A FILLER span is always emitted, but what it emits is whatever the record area held, and that differs by path. The two DALYTRAN rows and the account row carry 20 and 178 SPACES because the fixture rows carry spaces there and nothing in the program touches them. The cross-reference row's 14 spaces are supplied once, at seed time, by the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation. The category-balance row carries 22 ZERO CHARACTERS, not spaces: tcatbal.txt ships them as zeros, :474's keyed read brought the whole 50-byte area in, :527 changed TRAN-CAT-BAL alone and :528 wrote the area back, so a read-modify-rewrite preserves the bytes it never touched. Writing spaces there would be a divergence, and case01 - whose transaction this is - pins the same 22 zeros. Contrast case02, case08 and case15, where the record is INITIALIZEd at :504 and created at :510 instead. THE 36-BYTE SEED IS DELIBERATE. cardxref.txt is the one fixture in the repository whose on-disk width deviates from its copybook, 36 against the declared 50, and the rows are seeded at 36 exactly as the fixture ships them (gate G16, risk R-F). The pad is centralised in FieldDiffer rather than baked into any case file, which is why no input row here is 50 bytes and no input row here carries a FILLER value. WHY THE FAILURE IS INJECTED RATHER THAN SEEDED. No arrangement of fixture data can make a sequential READ of a PS dataset report a permanent error: the refusal is a property of the backend and not of the records, and both seeded rows are complete, valid 350-byte copies of dailytran.txt rows 0 and 2, seeded inline so each row measures its own width - DatasetInput refuses a recordLength beside inline rows precisely so no second, unchecked opinion about a width can exist - precisely so that nothing about the data could be blamed for it. Record 2 is a real transaction - DALYTRAN-ID 0000000006292564, type 01, category 0001, +67.88 on card 6009619150674526 - and it is never processed, because the failure happens on the READ that would have delivered it and not on anything it contains. Nor is the arrangement expressible in this file: ForcedOutcome belongs to ParityCase.ScreenRequest, which ParityCase refuses for any unitKind other than CONTROLLER_POJO, so a BATCH_JOB case may not carry one. It therefore lives in CBTRN02CParityTest's own scenario table as DALYTRAN_READ_FAILS, scoped to the second read of this one dataset - the first read succeeds normally and returns record 1 - exactly as case07, case14 and case17 state their arrangements there. PROVENANCE AND STANDARDS. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED, by structured reading of app/cbl/CBTRN02C.cbl against the byte layouts of app/cpy/CVTRA06Y.cpy, CVTRA05Y.cpy, CVTRA01Y.cpy, CVACT01Y.cpy and CVACT03Y.cpy, the DD and DCB contracts of app/jcl/POSTTRAN.jcl, and the real rows of app/data/ASCII. It is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment; the provenance of the expected values is substituted and nothing else, so the case count, the field-for-field diffing and the zero-diff gate are all unchanged. Because that modifies a stated success criterion it is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than absorbed (AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A). review_rules reports that NO USER RULES were provided for this project, so the case is held to the AAP 0.10.2 enterprise practices instead, and their absence is not treated as licence to lower the bar: B1 no placeholders, both seeded rows and all three committed rows are complete records and the injected status is a specific two-character value; B3 the legacy sources and app/data are read-only and every seed row is a byte-exact copy; B5 the truncated tail and the surviving writes are preserved exactly rather than tidied into a graceful shutdown or a rollback; B7 deterministic, with TRAN-PROC-TS pinned at 2022-07-19-23.12.34.000000 from the harness clock and never a captured now; B8 explicit widths, channels and values throughout, every field enumerated at its full declared width; B11 the widths summed and the amounts re-derived from the raw zoned bytes above rather than asserted - 0000005047G is 0000005047 with a G overpunch, digit 7 positive, so +504.77, and 00000001930{ is 00000001930 with a { overpunch, digit 0 positive, so 193.00, whose sum is the 697.77 asserted here; and B12 this paragraph. HOW THE ARRANGEMENT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA: the backend behaviour this case runs under used to be held in a twenty-entry Java map keyed by this file's case identifier, which meant the file gave no indication whether it posted three hundred transactions or abended on a second read; renumbering it would have silently moved the arrangement to a different run; and a twenty-first case would have thrown from the lookup. A BATCH_JOB case genuinely cannot carry a ForcedOutcome - that member belongs to ParityCase.ScreenRequest, which a batch case may not declare - but unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes is declarable by every unit kind and exists for exactly this, so the arrangement is now stated here beside the seed. Silence is itself a declaration: a case that names no call site runs entirely on its seeded rows. This case declares READ-DALYTRAN reporting FILE STATUS '30' after one record - the access method's permanent error on the SECOND READ DALYTRAN-FILE at app/cbl/CBTRN02C.cbl:346, which is the only way the third arm of the guard at :347-356 can ever be taken: a sequential read of a physical-sequential dataset refuses because of the backend and never because of the records. afterRecords 1 scopes it to the second read deliberately - the first succeeds and delivers a record the run posts in full, so the case asserts both that the failure happened and that what preceded it survived. Arranging the refusal at the JDBC layer instead would refuse the open too and the run would never reach the read.
